propositions: Completion verification currently materializes the full Git-backed ticket store despite reading only a small subset, causing 135–235 seconds in close traces.

Close path publishes PASS COMPLETION_VERDICT, STATUS update, and completion SIGNATURE through separate writes, allowing durable PASS to outlive a failed close and a closed ticket to outlive a failed signature.
New pinned-ticket reader must resolve arbitrary IDs/aliases/Jira bindings at tickets_oid without fallback to live state, recording negative reads and maintaining typed separation from code_oid.

Atomicity requirement: one committed-store transaction must contain PASS sidecar, closed STATUS, and completion SIGNATURE together, or none committed; OID-pinned readers see complete old or complete new state.
Before mutation, receipt from prior state A must validate against current descendant Tn; conflicts on ticket/global paths discard verdict and restart, while unrelated changes may continue.
Completion path operates behind a configuration switch with legacy path retained as explicit back-out; default enablement is evidence-based and fixed at operation start without silent fallback.
